review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of the apply lemmas and membership lemmas. The simp set is small: factoredNumbers_empty, smoothNumbers_zero, smoothNumbers_one and four equiv-apply lemmas. I found no loops or competing normal forms. The *_eq_factoredNumbers lemmas are correctly left out of simp. The one real issue is the redundant pair of simp lemmas for each equivalence. I did not check, by running Lean, that dropping the specialised lemmas leaves every downstream simp call working. The only external uses of these lemmas I found (Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/Basic.lean, lines 100 and 107) rewrite with the primed version.

findings.excerpt: equivProdNatFactoredNumbers hp hs (e, ⟨m, hm⟩) = p ^ e * m := rfl
findings.problem: Each equivalence has two @[simp] apply lemmas that rewrite the same term. The specialised lemma is for a pair written as (e, ⟨m, hm⟩). The primed lemma is for an arbitrary x : ℕ × factoredNumbers s. The primed one subsumes the specialised one: after instantiating x := (e, ⟨m, hm⟩), the projections reduce by simp to p ^ e * m. So the specialised lemma adds nothing to the simp set except another candidate for the discrimination tree. Which rule fires depends on the shape of the argument. The same duplication appears in the smooth-number version at lines 374–380. The only downstream uses I found (EulerProduct/Basic.lean lines 100 and 107) rewrite with the primed lemma. The unprimed one is not used anywhere in Mathlib.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one canonical simp lemma per equivalence, the primed general one (equivProdNatFactoredNumbers_apply' and equivProdNatSmoothNumbers_apply'). Either drop @[simp] from the pair-specific lemmas or delete them. If they are kept for rw convenience, say so in a docstring. This relies on simp reducing (e, m).1 and (e, m).2, which it does with its built-in projection reduction. I have not run Lean to confirm.
findings.benefit: There is a single canonical simp rule per equivalence, so there are no overlapping rewrite rules and a smaller simp set. Readers also see which lemma is the intended interface.

evidence.excerpt: equivProdNatFactoredNumbers hp hs x = p ^ x.1 * x.2 := rfl
equivProdNatSmoothNumbers hp (e, ⟨m, hm⟩) = p ^ e * m := rfl
